abstract: Purpose: Deep learning-based medical image segmentation has achieved remarkable success, yet purely data-driven approaches often fail to exploit the rich mathematical structure inherent in medical images. Conclusion: M-Net establishes that mathematical inductive biases provide effective complementary information for medical image segmentation. The continuous condition-number feature offers superior gradient information over discrete alternatives, and MAG preserves these priors throughout the network. This work opens avenues for integrating linear algebra and vector calculus into deep architectures for medical imaging.

abstract: Vessels encapsulating tumor clusters (VETC) are an aggressive vascular phenotype of hepatocellular carcinoma that is usually determined after surgery. A foundation model-enabled framework for pathology-informed VETC prediction on pretreatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), termed PIVOT, uses paired preoperative multiparametric MRI, postoperative hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images, and CD34 immunohistochemistry during model development, while inference requires only preoperative MRI. PIVOT-MRI uses morphologic and vascular embedding alignment, and PIVOT-Clinical combines the PIVOT-MRI score with tumor size and alpha-fetoprotein. PIVOT-MRI achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.887 in the internal test cohort and 0.839-0.861 across external cohorts. PIVOT-Clinical increases the internal-test area under the curve to 0.904 and PIVOT-Clinical-defined groups are associated with different two-year recurrence risks. Removing both histopathologic alignment branches results in the largest ablation-related performance decrease. Exploratory radiotranscriptomic analyses showed that higher PIVOT-MRI scores were associated with angiogenesis-related, endothelial, and proliferative transcriptional programs. PIVOT enables noninvasive preoperative assessment of pathology-defined vascular aggressiveness in resectable hepatocellular carcinoma while preserving an MRI-only clinical inference pathway.

abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a nomogram for preoperative assessment of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) based on the radiological features of enhanced CT and to verify two imaging techniques (CT and MRI) in an external centre. The radiological features and clinical information of enhanced CT images were analysed, and the independent variables associated with MVI in HCC were determined by logistic regression analysis. No statistical difference in AUC values among training set and testing sets was found. CONCLUSION: The proposed nomogram prediction model for MVI in HCC has high accuracy, can be used with different imaging techniques, and has good clinical applicability.

abstract: Abstract Purpose Noninvasive preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a significant clinical challenge worldwide. Method Data were retrospectively examined for 115 consecutive patients (mean age: 57.2 ± 10.7 years; 95 men) who had undergone surgical resection for HCC (tumor diameter less than 3 cm). Peritumoral expansions (3 mm, 5 mm, and 10 mm) were generated from manually segmented intratumoral regions of interest (ROIs) across the arterial, venous, and delayed phases. We then evaluated the predictive performance of five encoding methods combined with four machine learning classifiers using both clinical characteristics and radiomics features. Result Multi-phase models incorporating temporal encoding methods consistently outperformed single-phase models and those relying solely on clinical characteristics. Conclusion While radiologists routinely monitor multi-phase contrast dynamics qualitatively, our findings demonstrate that these cross-phase variations provide quantifiable, highly predictive information for MVI. This framework represents a promising, noninvasive quantitative tool for preoperative MVI risk stratification.

title: Preoperative prediction of HCC microvascular invasion by multimodel peritumoral diffusion MRI
abstract: Abstract Objective Most studies emphasize intratumoral diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) metrics, but few studies have examined whether peritumoral DWI metrics can provide added value. We aimed to evaluate three-dimensional, multiscale, multimodel DWI parameters within intratumoral and peritumoral volumes of interest for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Materials and methods Seventy patients with HCC, including 42 with MVI, were prospectively enrolled. We calculated parameters from monoexponential, intravoxel incoherent motion, diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), stretched-exponential model (SEM), and continuous-time random-walk models within the tumor and in 3-mm (P3) and 5-mm (P5) peritumoral rims. Features showing differences on univariable analysis were further screened using logistic regression with variance inflation factor filtering to build combined models. Diagnostic performance was assessed by areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Results Four intratumoral diffusion-coefficient–related metrics showed significant differences between groups. In the peritumoral regions, 12 parameters differed between groups, including diffusion-coefficient–related indices and heterogeneity-related metrics. Among single parameters, P3_DKI_ K app achieved the best discrimination for MVI (AUROC = 0.713); P5_DKI_ K app and Tumor_SEM_DDC were selected as independent imaging predictors. After integrating alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and tumor size, the combined model (Cli-IntraPeriDWI) yielded the best performance (AUROC = 0.844). SHAP analysis indicated that higher AFP, larger tumor size, higher P5_DKI_ K app , and lower Tumor_SEM_DDC were associated with increased MVI risk. Conclusion Peritumoral DWI offers multiple biomarkers and outperforms intratumoral metrics for MVI prediction. An interpretable model integrating peritumoral and intratumoral DWI with clinical factors enables accurate, noninvasive preoperative MVI risk stratification in HCC. Key Points Question Can multiscale, multimodel peritumoral DWI metrics improve preoperative prediction of MVI in HCC compared with intratumoral DWI metrics? Findings Compared with intratumoral DWI, peritumoral DWI offered more potential imaging biomarkers and superior diagnostic capability for the preoperative diagnosis of MVI in HCC. Relevance statement By integrating intratumoral and peritumoral metrics with clinical risk factors, we developed a model achieving optimal performance and transparent decision interpretability for MVI assessment, supporting preoperative prognostic evaluation and individualized treatment planning in HCC.

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac MRE data alone demonstrated the feasibility of accurate LV myocardium segmentation, with nnU-Net and MedSAM both reaching inter-reader-level performance. These findings support direct segmentation of the LV myocardium from native cardiac MRE and represent a step toward a self-contained cardiac MRE workflow.

abstract: Achieving accurate Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) liver image segmentation is of great significance in the field of medicine. It assists doctors in rapidly locating a target region, aids treatment, and plays a key role in postoperative observation. Then, the extracted RoI region is data processed and fed into a downstream U-Net network for secondary segmentation, where special attention is paid to local information during the second segmentation to obtain finer prediction results. abstract: Rationale and objectives This study aims to develop a framework integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI)-based multi-channel deep learning combined with clinical modeling for the non-invasive preoperative discrimination between hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (MF-ICC). The independent external validation cohort included 50 patients, comprising 40 with HCC and 10 with MF-ICC. We constructed separate two-dimensional deep learning models based on arterial phase, portal venous phase, and delayed phase images and then developed fusion models (2D model). A multi-channel deep learning model was further developed by directly inputting the three-phase images stacked along the channel dimension. However, no significant differences in AUCs were found among the models after correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusion The fusion model integrating clinical predictors with DCE-MRI multi-phase deep learning feature may provide a valuable tool for preoperatively differentiating HCC from MF-ICC.

title: WavPAC-Net: a wavelet-based hybrid encoder network with permuted axial-channel feature enhancement for liver segmentation
abstract: The liver, core to human metabolism and detoxification, is threatened by chronic diseases like cirrhosis that increase hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk, with early diagnosis dependent on accurate liver segmentation in medical imaging. Current clinical segmentation methods generally suffer from low efficiency, strong subjectivity, and scarcity of AI-driven commercial products. Although deep learning technologies have been applied to liver segmentation, mainstream architectures still exhibit inherent limitations: CNN struggles with long-range dependencies while Transformer lacks fine detail representation. This study proposes WavPAC-Net, an innovative wavelet-based fusion network incorporating: (1) a hybrid CNN-Transformer encoder combining ConvNeXt-Small branch for precise hepatic parenchymal texture capture and Swin Transformer branch for long-range dependency modeling; (2) a Wavelet Domain Fusion Module (WDFM) that decomposes the features extracted by CNN and Transformer into low-frequency and high-frequency sub-bands respectively, and performs adaptive weighted fusion; and (3) a Permuted Axial-Channel Feature Enhancer (PACFE) that implements cross-dimensional refinement of high-dimensional fused features through collaborative three-dimensional spatial modeling and channel dimension permutation. In systematic comparisons with 20 state-of-the-art segmentation models, WavPAC-Net demonstrates statistically significant advantages in both segmentation accuracy and boundary fidelity. Evaluated on the CirrMRI600+ dataset (T2-weighted MRI), WavPAC-Net achieved Dice score of 93.16%, IoU of 88.45%, and MCC of 93.03%, with a computational complexity of 19.88 GFLOPs. Multi-modal validation on the public LiTS CT dataset further confirmed the model’s excellent performance, achieving Dice score of 96.91%, IoU of 94.32%, and MCC of 96.79%. Overall, WavPAC-Net provides an effective balance between segmentation accuracy and computational complexity, supporting its potential for practical liver segmentation applications.

title: Ideal Point Fusion for Reliable Morphometry of Lunar Regolith Particles
abstract: Lunar regolith particle morphology is critical for particle classification and representative sample selection. Morphometric measurements also provide key parameters for discrete element modeling and the development of regolith simulants with controlled particle shapes. However, their accuracy depends directly on segmentation quality. This study investigates whether combining measurements from complementary segmentation models can improve accuracy across morphological descriptors. The fusion leaves the source masks unchanged. The objective is to develop and evaluate Morphology-Aware Ideal-Point Fusion (MIPF). MIPF evaluates each model in three dimensions: region completeness, boundary accuracy, and false-positive suppression. Ideal-point analysis assigns higher scores to models closer to the best observed performance and farther from the worst. MIPF uses descriptor-specific weights for these scores to determine each model’s contribution. Area-based indices place more weight on region completeness, while contour-based indices emphasize boundary accuracy. MIPF then retains the two highest-weighted models and combines their measurements without generating a new mask. In a ground-truth comparison based on dataset-level means for 15 morphological indices, MIPF ranks first for six indices and second for the remaining nine, giving an average rank of 1.60. Its median relative error is 11.56%, compared with 12.96% for U-Mamba, 13.73% for nnU-Net, 15.30% for OffSeg, and 31.18% for SegFormer. Although MIPF does not minimize the error for every index, it achieves the most consistent overall performance and reduces the dependence of aggregate morphometric results on any single segmentation model.

abstract: Liver tumor detection from CT images is challenging because most CT slices do not contain tumors, while only a small number contain tumor regions. title: Advances in proton therapy technology and global clinical applications
abstract: Proton therapy, by leveraging its unique physical characteristic of the Bragg peak, enables high-precision dose delivery to the tumor target while effectively protecting surrounding normal tissues, and has become an important representative of advanced radiotherapy. Moving forward, it is essential to continue promoting technological integration and innovation, strengthen high-quality clinical research, and develop a more accessible, intelligent, and personalized proton therapy system to achieve broader clinical application and patient benefit.

abstract: Electroporation-based treatments rely on increasing the permeability of the cell membrane by high voltage electric pulses applied to tissue via electrodes. However, the average error of the automatic vessel segmentation did not have an impact on the electric field distribution if the central electrode was present. This suggests the algorithm is robust enough to be used in creating a model for treatment parameter optimization, but with a central electrode.

title: Unveiling the role of spatial transcriptomics in the analysis of the tumor immune microenvironment (Review)
abstract: The tumor immune microenvironment plays a decisive role in tumor initiation, progression and therapeutic response. Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables comprehensive analysis of the whole transcriptome or specific gene sets while preserving the original spatial location information within tissues, offering a revolutionary approach to unraveling the complexity of the tumor immune microenvironment in the spatial dimension. Focusing on tumor microenvironment niches at different stages of tumor progression, from precancerous lesions and locally advanced tumors to distant metastasis, recent advances in ST for mapping the spatial distribution and functional states of key cell subpopulations are summarized. The deep integration of machine learning with ST is laying a solid theoretical foundation and technical support for precision medicine and early intervention.
